clue.text: One may get bitter if one is used

definitions.text: One may get bitter if one is used

blocks.clueFragment: One may get bitter if one is used
blocks.note: surface reading: someone exploited by others may grow resentful
setter's reading: bitter is a British style of draught ale, drawn by the device used at a bar

explanation.surface: A warning that being exploited by others leaves a person resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' is not a mood but a pint: bitter is a hoppy British ale, pulled at the bar with a hand-operated device.
explanation.definitionFit: A barman works this hand-operated lever to draw cask ale such as bitter up from the cellar.

clue.text: Grow into suit

blocks.note: first meaning: develop into, turn into over time
second meaning: look good on, flatter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a child growing into a hand-me-down suit; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to develop into something and to flatter or look right on someone, as a hat might.

clue.text: Make possible arrest, breaking Helen's heart

indicators.note: the heart of a name is its inside, so the outer letters of the name are dropped
one word breaking another splits it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: the name without its first and last letters
to nab is to catch or arrest

explanation.surface: Someone is told that a police arrest breaking Helen's heart will make something possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' reads as emotion in the surface, but here it trims the name down to its inner letters, which the arrest then splits.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable something is to give the means or opportunity for it to happen, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Nut, as I chop it, changes shape

indicators.note: the phrase that changes shape is remoulded, so its letters take a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A cook watches a nut alter as they chop it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The pistachio is a green-kernelled nut from a tree native to western Asia, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Famous sculptor I challenge, unwisely, in Missouri

indicators.note: something done unwisely is done badly, so the letters come out in a muddled order
the shuffled words are placed inside the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri
the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly picks a fight with a celebrated sculptor in the American state of Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters sit between the M and O of the state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo carved the David and the Pietà, making him one of the best-known sculptors of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Mischievous member - is husband following one?

indicators.note: following tells us the earlier words come after the one named last, fixing the order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a Member of Parliament
taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a mischievous family member is the husband trailing after someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: An impish child behaves like a little imp, playfully naughty, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Fruit - piece to be consumed

blocks.note: a chess or draughts piece is a man
to go is to be used up, as money goes

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is set out ready to be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' looks like a slice of the fruit but is a game piece; 'go' means be used up, as in 'the food will soon go'.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a sweet tropical stone fruit, so it is an instance of the general word.

clue.text: Decidedly trendy black suit

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable
spades is one of the two black suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A fashion verdict that a black suit is definitely in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' is clothing on the surface but a card suit in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something in spades is having it in abundance, an idiom meaning to a marked or decided degree.

clue.text: Impeded female deer, wild deer

indicators.note: a wild animal runs loose, so its letters run out of order

blocks.note: a hind is a female red deer
the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A doe and a wild stag get in each other's way.
explanation.definitionFit: To hinder is to obstruct or hold back, so the past tense matches the past participle of impede.

clue.text: Outstanding performer, girl in plant ignoring us

indicators.note: ignoring two letters means leaving them out of the word they belong to
the first word is placed inside the trimmed word that follows

blocks.note: a cactus is a desert plant
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A star performer and a girl are found among plants, with the rest of us left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring us' is literal: the two letters U and S are dropped from the plant before the girl goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A class act is someone of real quality, especially an excellent entertainer or sports player.

clue.text: Son appearing in club concert

indicators.note: something appearing in another thing turns up inside it

blocks.note: a union is a club or association
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son plays a club gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' looks like a musical event, but it means agreement, as in 'acting in concert'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert and acting in unison both mean doing things together in agreement, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Fashionable sophisticate, but not a woman, surprisingly

indicators.note: an outcome that comes surprisingly is unexpected, so the letters land in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A stylish sophisticate turns out, to everyone's surprise, not to be female.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder neatly hints at the answer's first word, since a man is not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A man about town is a worldly socialite seen at every fashionable venue, an idiom for an urbane gentleman.

clue.text: Country producing whisky, Africa's first

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the continent's name is wanted

blocks.note: a malt is a malt whisky
the opening letter of the continent

explanation.surface: A nation that makes whisky is named as Africa's leading producer.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean, south of Sicily, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Complex lecture by the Spanish sailor

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
an AB is an able seaman
to orate is to make a formal speech

explanation.surface: A complicated lecture is given by a sailor from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue as lecture, then the Spanish sailor; 'by' places the lecture after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate has many detailed parts, so it is intricate or complicated, a synonym.

clue.text: Country folk look round hydrogen plant

indicators.note: one word going round another wraps it, holding it inside

blocks.note: peasants are rural labourers
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Rural people inspect a hydrogen plant, a factory making the gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as an industrial works but is the flower; H sits after the P of PEASANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasant's eye is a flowering plant, the name used for a red-flowered adonis and for a narcissus, so it is an example.

clue.text: Loaf of bread, key kitchen item?

blocks.note: a tin is a loaf baked in an oblong tin
a key is something that opens a lock

explanation.surface: Bread is named as an essential in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a tin, or tin loaf, is a rectangular loaf of bread. The question mark flags the playful reading of key.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin-opener is a hand tool kept in a kitchen drawer for cutting the lids off cans.

clue.text: Female's stretching across bed with cold drinks

indicators.note: something stretching across another spans it, so it sits on both sides of it

blocks.note: she's, a female's
a cot is a small bed
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A woman lies sprawled across a bed with some chilled drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Female's' hides 'she is', which splits after its first letter to wrap the bed and the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotches are measures of whisky distilled in Scotland, so each is an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Negligence round embassy

blocks.note: the letter O is round in shape
a diplomatic mission is an embassy

explanation.surface: Carelessness is alleged around a foreign embassy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a container signal but simply supplies the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is a failure to do something, so it is a near synonym for neglect or negligence.

clue.text: Shared views in popular stadium

blocks.note: common means widespread or of the people
a sports ground is a stadium

explanation.surface: Fans in a well-loved stadium find they agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Common ground is the area of opinion two sides agree on, an idiom for beliefs held jointly.

clue.text: Station American in English college

indicators.note: the first part is put inside the word that follows

blocks.note: Eton College is a famous English public school
US, as in United States

explanation.surface: An American student is placed at a college in England.
explanation.walkthrough: EUSTON is a London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is one of London's main railway terminals, serving trains to the north-west, so it is an example of a station.

clue.text: Ms du Maurier had pen repaired?

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the novelist had her pen mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier was the English novelist who wrote Rebecca, so the given name fits the title and surname.

clue.text: Airman up for trial?

blocks.note: surface reading: an air force man facing a court case
setter's reading: a flier whose job is trying out new aircraft, up in the air

explanation.walkthrough: 'Up for trial' suggests a courtroom; read literally, the airman is up in the sky, flying for trials of a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of pilot flies new or modified aircraft to assess their performance and safety.

clue.text: Gather fuel around lake

indicators.note: one word placed around another encloses it

blocks.note: peat is dug and burnt as fuel
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone collects fuel from around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' is a dressmaking term here, not collecting.
explanation.definitionFit: In sewing, to gather fabric is to draw it into folds, as one does when making a pleat.

clue.text: Friend describing university to a girl

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so this word goes round the next

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
U is the standard abbreviation for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend tells a girl all about university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing around.
explanation.definitionFit: Paula is a woman's first name, and crosswords use girl to define any female given name.

clue.text: Young cow provided that in here somehow

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some unspecified way, so the word's letters are rearranged
the first part is put inside the scrambled word that follows

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
if means on condition that

explanation.surface: A young cow is said to be around here somewhere, provided that someone looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young female bovine that has not yet had a calf, the farming term for this animal.

clue.text: To better score is excellent

blocks.note: to top is to beat or outdo
to score is to cut a notch, and a notch is a tally mark

explanation.surface: A boast that beating a score would be excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an informal adjective for first-rate or of the highest quality, a synonym.

clue.text: Piece of classical music from Brahms on at arena

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken straight out of the run of words after it

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the composer's name and the next three words

explanation.surface: A Brahms work is being played at an arena concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a classical composition for one or two instruments in several movements, a type of musical piece.

clue.text: Charm one's way in?

blocks.note: first meaning, a verb stressed on the second syllable: to delight or bewitch
second meaning, a noun stressed on the first syllable: a door or gateway

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests charming one's way into somewhere; the two halves are separate meanings, said differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning to fill with wonder and a noun for the opening through which one enters.
